name: Direct Surface Rendering with Intersection Buffer
definition: A rendering technique that casts rays into a volume to find all surface intersections, storing them in an intersection buffer. This allows interactive cutting operations without retracing rays, by using depth buffers derived from cutting planes to select the correct intersection via comparison.
summary: Direct Surface Rendering with Intersection Buffer stores all ray-surface intersections per pixel to enable interactive cutting without re-tracing rays or pre-computing meshes.
